reviews.text: Visiting Shanghai Disneyland honestly exceeded my expectations. The park feels bigger and more open than I imagined, and the castle is stunning both during the day and at night — especially once it’s lit up. What stood out to me most was how immersive everything felt. The details in each area are very well done, and even just walking around felt enjoyable. The rides are a good mix of fun and impressive, not just for kids but for adults as well. Compared to other Disney parks I’ve been to, this one feels newer and more spacious. Crowds were manageable when I went, and the overall experience felt smooth and well organized. Definitely worth a full day, and I’d recommend staying until nighttime to see the park in a completely different atmosphere.

We visited Shanghai Disneyland in mid-November and it exceeded all my expectations. The weather was very cold, and we queued for about an hour before the official park opening. To our surprise, the park opened earlier than the stated time, which was a great start to the day. Because of that, we managed to ride TRON Lightcycle Power Run with almost no wait — and it was absolutely the best ride I’ve ever experienced. Truly next level. My second favourite ride was Seven Dwarfs Mine Train — fun, smooth, and beautifully themed. Overall, the park operations were impressive. People generally queued patiently, everyone was polite, and we didn’t experience any queue cutting, which made the experience very pleasant. We spent two full days in the park and were able to cover most of the rides without feeling too rushed. The park is well designed, immersive, and magical in its own way. We loved it so much and will definitely be back again. Highly recommended! ✨🎢

This Disneyland park is notably the most expansive we have encountered. The selection of attractions is exceptional, ranging from Tron to the immersive Pirates of the Caribbean. Our children particularly enjoyed the Zootopia theme park. Numerous photo opportunities are available, and the Hot Pursuit ride offers a truly remarkable experience. We advise guests to be aware of potential wait times. Nevertheless, a visit to this park is highly recommended if you are in Shanghai.

Overall, Shanghai Disneyland is a great park, and it is entirely possible to cover every zone in a single day, especially if you visit during a good weather month like November and utilize Premier Access. ​Highlights and Attractions ​Rides for Everyone: The attractions at SDL are generally well-suited for families and children, as they are generally not too scary. You can manage to hit all the key rides across the park's seven zones in one day. ​TRON is a Must: The TRON Lightcycle Power Run was a personal favorite and is highly recommended. ​The Power of Premier Access: Using Premier Access (for around five key attractions like TRON, Soaring Over the Horizon, and Zootopia: Hot Pursuit, as noted in the plan) was crucial for successfully fitting everything into the one-day visit. ​Entertainment and Atmosphere ​Spectacular Nighttime Shows: The evening entertainment is a major highlight. The fireworks and the night parade (like the Disney Winter Magic Cavalcade and Illuminate! A Nighttime Celebration) are described as very beautiful and should not be missed. ​Logistics and Practical Tips ​Convenient Travel: Traveling to the park is very convenient, as you can easily get there by taking the Metro. ​Food and Drink Policy: It is helpful that visitors can bring outside food and drinks into the park. ​Bag Check Warning: Be prepared for a very long bag check process. They do not use scanning machines; bags are checked manually by staff, which significantly slows down entry. ​Constructive Feedback ​Cast Member Friendliness: One area for improvement is the staff. The Cast Members were not as cheerful or friendly compared to the staff at other international theme parks visited. ​Food Quality: The food inside the park is expensive, and the taste is quite mediocre—it’s not particularly impressive.

We went on Jan 5th, 2026 and it was not too crowded. We finished all the attractions by 8Pm (we arrived at 8.30 am) :)) the longest waiting time is Tron is 75 minutes (compared to crowded season is 2 hours).The facilities, especially toilet is good, no need to worry. Pirates of Carribean is very good :)) we love all the details. It is always fun time visit any Disneyland places (LA, Tokyo, Hongkong, Shanghai. I have not visited one in Orlando and Paris).

I visited Shanghai Disneyland for the first time, and it was an amazing experience. While it is smaller compared to other Disneyland parks around the world and doesn’t have as many rides, it still offers a very well,designed and enjoyable experience. Because it’s located in Shanghai, it attracts a large local crowd, but the park is well managed and organised. The service throughout the park was excellent,staff were friendly, helpful, and professional. The rides were genuinely fun, with TRON Lightcycle Power Run being the absolute highlight and a must-try attraction. Food options were also better than expected, with good variety and quality. Overall, for my first-ever Disneyland visit, it was a fantastic choice and definitely worth visiting.

Please get the early pass totally worth it! Manage to ride the tron 3 times!! Download the Disneyland Shanghai apps. Really helpful especially the maps and the showtime. Get the pawsicle in Zootopia. It is so good! Not much food for Muslim so bring RTE. Toilets were clean but no bidet. Many water stations to refill your bottle. The water taste fine, no weird taste at all.

Largest and newest Disney park globally. Crowded. Some rides had a wait time >200 mins during our December visit. Popular rides were consistently >60 mins wait. Disney hotel patrons has early park access each day. Food is notably better than other parks, including Tokyo Disney. Staff service inconsistent, we overheard staff raising voices at patrons. Queue cutting not commonplace, but did occur on few occasions. Designated outdoor smoking area at sections of the park, with smell spreading to neighbouring areas. Squat toilet in park washrooms. Limited dining opportunities in Disney Town after park closes at night.

One of the best Disneyland experiences we’ve had to date. I’ve been to a few Disney parks around the world, and this one is by far my favorite. We rode about 90% of the attractions with wait times of 30 minutes or less on a weekday, all without a FastPass. One thing to note: tripods and selfie sticks aren’t allowed, but they’ll let you store them in a locker instead of confiscating them. Overall, a very memorable visit

If you love Disney, you should definitely visit the world's largest Disneyland. Be prepared to walk around 20,000 steps a day! We visited during a public holiday and had been monitoring the crowd calendar in advance. Based on the crowd predictions, we decided to purchase the Early Entry pass (still, we came around 5 am) and stayed at a nearby hotel. Thanks to this, we were able to ride all the major attractions on our list. Vegetarian options are available, though the selection is limited. Sadly, the staff were not as friendly as those at Disneyland Japan.

Good fun. The queues are quite long though. Most of the popular attractions are over 100 minutes wait time. We did find that the line went quicker than they anticipated. A lot of the attractions which were 5 min wait time were pleasant to do as an adult. We had no kids with us, just 3 adults. Queue to get into the park took almost one hour to get in, the one nice thing is you are constantly moving, not standing still all the time. To get your ticket, you need ID, so if a foreigner remember to take your passport. At the gate they scan your passport and then you go through. Super easy. When you leave Disneyland it is not clear where to get didi. Its not the same place that you get dropped off. When you come out of the park, go straight over the foot bridge, dont go right to where the taxis are. Overall we had a really nice time. If you dont plan to spend the whole day there, id suggest going in the afternoon around 3pm. 5 - 6 hours is enough, especially if you dont plan to go on all the rides. If you go on all the rides, you'll need around 6 - 8 hours to stand in queues.

Loved my Disney Shanghai experience! Visited in November on a Monday which was moderately busy. Longer wait times for the popular rides however it was bearable. Definitely start with Zootopia followed by Tron. Was able to knock out all the rides before the fireworks show in the evening.

Visiting Shanghai Disneyland was an unforgettable experience! The park is vibrant, full of energy, and bursting with color—especially thanks to all the amazing cosplay. Guests dressed up in creative costumes really brought the magic to life and made the atmosphere even more festive. From thrilling rides to enchanting shows, there’s something for everyone to enjoy. I highly recommend booking your tickets in advance to avoid long lines and make the most of your visit. Whether you’re a Disney fan or just looking for a fun day out, Shanghai Disneyland is a must-see destination!

Been there on a Monday. Priority pass recommended. 🌟Food is really good, especially compared to other Theme Parks in the Western World. Sizes perfect. 🌟Service stellar, as expect from our Asian friends. 🌟Clean everywhere.

Visited from 11am to 9:30pm on a Thursday and only completed 5 rides for the entire visit, this is the busiest park in all of Asia with close to 50k people everyday with all of the good rides your waiting for 1-2 hours (Tron, pirates, flying) just spend the money and buy the express pass, we had 6 in our party and it would of been $1000 to upgrade and it was the last park for us to visit from around the world so we just waited it out since we already been to all the parks. The park is built for large crowds, huge walkways and lots of land beautifully landscaped. Different types of strange foods with a few classics like the turkey leg but you can bring in a backpack with waters, canned coffee and snacks without any kind of hassle from the security check point. Very clean, well run with plenty of staff to maintain the masses with workers staged throughout the lines to make sure there is no line cutting because the lines are enormous!

Superb place for the family, a definite recommendation for anyone visiting Shanghai, loads of things to do and some awesome rides including pirates 3D ride and zootopia which were absolutely fun, the place is huge and definitely need 2 days to cover all rides but if you come early and on weekdays you can do many rides. Access to the place is easy and with didi app you can go to book for as much as a 120 yuan from city center or take a metro ride. Food is normal and overpriced as expected so suggest you to take some snacks and drinks. Overall a fantastic experience.

Memorable experience, Zootopia area is my favorite. The land is beautifully designed and really makes you feel like you’ve stepped into the movie. the storybook castle is stunning and truly iconic. While crowds and wait times can be long, the overall atmosphere, shows, and attention to detail make the visit memorable and worth it.

The park is quite big, the facilities is very new. There's many water dispenser so do bring your own bottles. The park is easily accessible through the mrt. There's some shop outside the park to buy some finger food. The food and drink inside the park is Disney price. Do arrive early for the security screening. For foreigner the ticket is tied to our passport. Most of the ride is explain in mandarin. Weather can be hot in summer, do bring a cap, umbrella and perhaps a portable fan.

I am very happy, everything is wonderful. This is the dream place I have wanted to visit for a long time. I also really enjoyed the parade... and the fireworks display was extraordinary... thank you, I hope I can come again.

I went on a weekday, but there were still a lot of visitors. The line to enter the park was quite long and took a while. There’s a bag check before entering (and it was a bit odd to see that some people weren’t allowed to bring in certain items, while others seemed to get them through). The lines for the rides were also long, depending on which attraction you choose. If you don’t want to wait too long, you can buy special passes. Even though the regular queues take time, the overall crowd management is quite good. The park is also clean. Overall, it was a fun experience, but you may need to plan your rides and timing if you want to get through everything you want.

Absolutely fantastic holiday full of smiles and laughter. staff really friendly and helpful. Food was fabulous loving the character shaped food. The characters and parades are a must to smile, clap and wave to all your favourite characters . Holiday of joy.

Despite it being blazing hot and disgusting Shanghai Disneyland met this Disney Parks addict’s expectations. The park size was tolerable to get everything done in a day. The washrooms were clean and AC’d and had real toilets since we don’t do the squat thing. We were disappointed the parade became an “express” version due to the heat and literally was one float but I guess the heat might kill the workers in the costumes. There were some nice rides that were unique to the park. I was a bit disappointed there wasn’t a traditional Main St USA like Paris or WDW. Zootopia World blew me away. The imagineering that went into that is spectacular. The ride was a high thrill and super fun. Too bad the line ups are huge to get simple things like a popcorn bucket. Fireworks were great but I was surprised there were no drones like the Paris show! The theater show only had the songs in English not sure what they were saying. Theatre is quite large and reminded us of Disney Cruise Line theaters.

We had loads of fun at Shanghai Disneyland. Love their informative app - it offers realtime wait time feature👍😄 Also like their “favorite” feature for marking our favorite attractions💖🎈We were able to watch Mickey’s Storybook Express (parade) and enjoyed - The Many Adventures of Winnie the Pooh 小熊维尼历险记 - Zootopia Hot Pursuit - Voyages of the Crystal Grotto 孟彩奇航 - Mickey’s Storybook Adventure (theatre show) - Mickey’s Storybook Adventure (ride) - Hunny Pot Spin Their store’s products are cheaper than the ones in the US, in average😄😬 Their parades are at 12:15 and 3:45pm, instead of at night. We also enjoyed the fantastic fireworks and light shows - all in all, we had a fun-filled day and magical experience🥰💕🙌✨🎉

We had stayed in Toy Story Hotel They provided a shuttle busy to Disney town There was a very short line Had bought tickets online They check the passports and issue the tickets We had plenty of fun Was magical Waiting time varied depending on the ride from 10 minutes to 100 minutes but we had the chance to get on alot of rides We had difficult time searching for halal food i. Disney park all snacks/food offered was not halal In Disney town we found Cheese cake factory which had halal options

Visited Shanghai Disneyland in mid Jan 2026 and it was cold. Rare chance to experience snow at the park. Rides were awesome. Stayed at Toy Story Hotel with free shuttle bus and priority access. My kids loved the Zootopia ride. Will surely come again.

Very large park, quite a long walk to get into the park and to the tickets gates. Maps are only available on the park website, which is not really convenient to use. Attraction are good but there is always a long wait in queue.

WOW, what an unforgettable experience! Shanghai Disneyland is a dream come true for Disney fans of all ages. The park is beautifully designed, with stunning architecture and landscaping that immerses you in the Disney magic. The attractions and shows are top-notch, with plenty of thrilling rides and spectacular entertainment options. What impressed me most was the attention to detail and the Chinese cultural elements incorporated into the park. It's clear that the park is designed to delight both Disney fans and locals alike. If you're a Disney fan or just looking for a fun day out, Shanghai Disneyland is a must-visit destination. Don't miss it!"

It's fun. Logs of people and lots of of queuing. Download the Disney app and this helps to tell you the queue time or if you want to fast track, it is, expect to pay RMB180 per person. Tron and pirates of the Caribbean is my favourite and enjoyed it. Just a word of caution, DO NOT BRING ANY CAMERA WITH TRIPOD even if it the camera is handheld and can be converted into a tripod. The security will ask you to rent a locker RMB10 and pick it up at the end of the day.

One checked out from the wishlist! We're lucky to go to a low-crowd weekdays so we can ride many popular attractions (sometimes twice!), seeing both the parade and christmas parade, finally closing the day with beautiful fireworks

A trip down to Shanghai Disneyland, not that we love the rides but more of discovery, whats the difference between this and others. Crowd was alright, no isssues with entering the park but the queue for the rides were still very long. #china #shanghai #disneyland

Definitely never go back there very crowded. No one speak English everything very expensive wasted all my day and money not recommended securities are very rude. We had to wait two hours to get in and another two hours to just get to the other show we couldn’t get any rides. It is not worth it. John waste your time specially if you have kids they will be disappointed.

An amazing day at Shanghai Disneyland! Loved Pirates of the Caribbean, Roaring Rapids, and Soaring Over the Horizon. TRON Lightcycle Power Run was the best ride, and the fireworks at night were simply unforgettable!" 🎢🎇

Went to the park early on a weekday and we were able to get on most rides before noon basically all walk on. In the afternoon and after 5pm things got busier and so had to plan more - but by then we were just watching shows and parades. The Pirates ride is very unique from other parks, Zootopia is amazing and should be a morning priority, the food through the park is my only complaint (not bad, just not good). But if you plan (and have some good shoes) you can do the park in a day, or if want to move more casually then a day and a half.

The latest disney park to open and the first to open in mainland china. It is the largest single disney theme park in the world. Themed areas includes: Mickey's Avennue, Gardens of Imaginations, Tomorrowland, Toy Story Land, Fantasyland, Treasure Cove, Adventure Isle, and the latest expansion, Zootopia. Rides ranges from high-trill roller coasters, 4D animations, 3D animetronic rides, to mini coasters and caraosels. Perfectly suitable for chilldren, height requirements varies with the highest minimum height of 122cm. Also offera a lot of food varieties ranging from oriental to western style cuisine,such as noodles, rice dish, soups, dumplings, burgers, pizzas. While also offers a wide varieties of snacks and desserts properly distributed towards the park. Prices for entry ticket, annual passes, merchandises, food and beverages and services are relatively cheap compared to other Disneyland parks in the world. Recommended visited time of the week should be weekdays, and off-peak months since the ticket is usually cheaper and waiting time for rides and attraction are relatively quick, Beware though as the park does not allow customers to bring selfie sticks or extenders There is also seasonal decoration, merchandise, meet and greet, special shows and events in rotations which follows the seasonal change of the local climate.

Amazing park, very well devolved, variety of attractions, my only concern is the ride time, we line up 60 minutes for Rex's Racer and the ride run for 50 seconds, we line up for Jet Packs for another 60 minutes and the ride run for 60 seconds, maybe because it was a public holiday they reduce the ride time. Another concern is the fireworks, it definitely needs to be imporved.
I visited Shanghai Disneyland Resort on 28 November 2025 and the experience is one of the best I ever had. The Pirates of the Caribbean performance and The Zootopia ride was excellent.

totally worth the experience! lot of fun rides🎢 ; some must-try are pirates of carribean, 7 dwarfs mine train, & Tron. I love how they're putting alot of effort on decorations & everything so accurate close to the actual film🎬 u actually can go out and re-enter the park to save money for foods bc inside is soo overpriced for me personally (tbh its design rlly cute). otherwise u're also allowed to bring outside foods & drinks as long as it's not too stinky, I'm bringing sandwiches & some main course foods from familymart🥪🍙🍝 transport🚇 take metro line 11 to Disney Resort Station, walk ±4-5min tips : I'm visiting in June which is summer & it's rlly hot🥵 I suggest u to bring UV umbrellas & portable fan while waiting (except u have fastpass)

My wife and I have been fortunate enough to visit all Disney parks in the world (LA, Orlando, Paris, Hong Kong, Tokyo and Shanghai) and we visited this park last. We had a great time and it’s probably our favorite park in Asia. Maybe the one in Tokyo is superior because we’re both fans of the Hollywood Tower of Terror and this isn’t at the Shanghai park unfortunately. It does however have some cool attractions like Tron and the Pirates of the Caribbean. They were spectacular! I recommend arriving early and buying the fast passes if possible, some rides had wait times of up to 60 minutes (we visited the park in September) so buying the fast passes were a lifesaver.

After visiting Disneyland and Universal Studios in Singapore, Japan, Korea, Europe, and Hong Kong, I can confidently say that this has been the worst theme park experience I’ve had — and it is not worth the money spent. Almost every attraction requires a minimum queue of 30 minutes, with many rides taking up to 105 minutes or more. This clearly shows that the park capacity and ride facilities are insufficient to handle the number of visitors allowed inside. Despite paying a high entrance fee, the experience is dominated by long waiting times, overcrowding, and poor crowd control. In comparison, other Disney and Universal parks manage visitor flow far more effectively through better space planning, ride distribution, and queue management. I spent 8 days in Shanghai, and unfortunately, this was the most disappointing experience of the entire trip.

Disney is always overcrowded and hot temperatures are unavoidable in Disney reviews but unless you’re willing to triple your price of a visit with Fast passes, you’re in for a long day of line standing. Also there are far fewer rides than any Disney park so the lines get longer with less options available. Plus the walk from the metro to the park, then the long line for bag checks is horrible. I got blisters. We love Disney parks but this one is close to the bottom but it was fun to visit. Probably won’t be back as we live in US but overall fun.
Good time visiting there! It’s huge and long waiting line but I bought the fast pass. It was way so much easier. Recommend for online purchases.

Happy Place.. I really enjoyed being at Disneyland... but I didn't like the long lines... because we didn't buy fast track tickets. However, the lines were orderly and fairly quick. The restrooms were clean, and the staff were constantly cleaning. Drinking water refills were plentiful. There were several restaurants, and the food was quite good, especially for Disneyland prices. The must-see attractions were Zootopia and Tron, as they're probably only available at Shanghai Disneyland. The fireworks were cool and spectacular.
Had visited on New Year’s Eve and it was really quite crowded as expected but there was quite allot of rides that were still available to ride and not really long wait overall really fun I would say.

When you are so excited to start your Disneyland adventure but it will take you at least a 30-minute walk to get through the entrance from the parking lot to another 15-minute slow maze line to have your bags get inspected. Just by entering alone is already an hour waste of energy and time. It's still a 3 star because what matters to me is the experience well spent with family. It is not advisable to visit in the month of July though because it's too hot, like burning hot. I have used SPF 150 to avoid sunburn, but it didn't work at all.

One of the best Disneyland! Very big and spacious. Distance between each attraction is quite long. There restaurants and shops right outside. Queue is not bad though. I waited around 45-60 mins for the top rides such as Zootopia, Tron, Soaring. For less popular one, around 10-30 mins Overall, very good experience as always
When during halloween 🎃. Advices get a butler, if you want to try everything best 3 days during event, weather change out fast do take note night was 12*

Shanghai Disneyland Park is truly magical and full of unforgettable experiences. The park is beautifully designed, blending classic Disney charm with Chinese culture. The Enchanted Storybook Castle is breathtaking, and the nighttime fireworks show is simply spectacular. Rides like TRON Lightcycle Power Run and Pirates of the Caribbean: Battle for the Sunken Treasure are world-class and a must-try. The parades, live shows, and character encounters bring so much joy for both kids and adults. Staff are friendly and helpful, and there are plenty of food options even though it's not so tasty. A perfect place to create lasting memories – highly recommended!

The rides are fun but the crowds kinda reduce the quality of the experience. The fast track is convenient but it's not cheap. Be mindful of the food vouchers if you have any - you may have to spend more than the value of the voucher to be able to use it. For example, my voucher was worth around 100Y and I was told that I had to spend more than that amount to receive that discount e.g. 101Y. Also, the travel from the drop off point to the actual entrance of the park is so long. The ticket area is also inconsiderate of the disabled or elderly - there was no solution/fast track for these customers who had to walk through the busy, long and windy way to the ticket area (look at image). The effort placed into each theme of the park is impressive though.

This is a huge park. There is a lot of space to accomodate one of the most populous countries in the world. For such a huge park, there is a definite lack of attractions. Compared to other Disney parks we have been to, our visit to Shanghai Disney was by far the shortest. On the other hand, what you get here, you will not experience in other Disneys.

Splurged for early access and fast pass package as we had friends scare us that the waits would be excessive…… 60-120 minutes depending on ride for normal lines. Overall Zootopia rides were amazing…. Pirates of the Caribbean was 10/10. Way way better than US Disney ride

I had such a great time at Shanghai Disneyland. The park was clean, well-organized, and filled with amazing attractions that made the whole day exciting from start to finish. I especially loved the big Enchanted Storybook Castle, it’s absolutely stunning and even more magical in person. The fireworks show at night was the perfect ending to the day, beautiful and unforgettable. I got my tickets from Klook, and the process was really easy and convenient. Overall, I truly enjoyed my visit and would love to come back again.

I've been to all the other Disneyland parks in the world and this one definitely seems like a counterfeit. It is not nearly the same quality you'd find in Disney World. The staff here are very rude, never smile and are never helpful. I can't believe any real Disney park would allow everyone to smoke anywhere in front of all the kids without restriction. Everything seems chaotic with the crowd management and nothing is done to prevent people from budding in line, smoking anywhere or peeing in the bush. The thick accent English instructions is not understandable. Just to enter the park, they make you walk about 2 KMs, even though there wasn't that big of a queue. The attractions are of lower quality compared to USA, Tokyo and Paris. The food is what you would expect from a plaza food court while charging 4x the price. The park is not that big so there's no need to come right when it opens if you want to see the fireworks. I arrived around 8am and was done by 5pm. Had to sit around 4 hours to wait for the fireworks at 9:15pm. There is definitely nothing magical about this place. Pass...

Once in a lifetime experience. We visited the park for our 7 year old but it was my wife and myself who enjoyed it more, reliving our childhood. The park is very neat and clean. We had bought the entry tickets on Klook app and the check-in procedure was easy. The park was crowded for a week day but still we enjoyed! We arrived there at 11.30 am and the queue was fast moving. There is a Cheesecake factory outlet inside the park which was amazing! Remember to buy the Disney Photo pass which is affordable and convenient.

Shanghai Disneyland is a magical place with so many things to explore. The park is very big, so wear comfy shoes! Everything looks lovely and well-designed, perfect for photo spots. Prices are a bit expensive, but the experience is worth it. Overall, a fun and memorable visit for all ages!

Despite the high ticket price, the experience was disappointing. We had to queue for over an hour just to enter — and that’s before the attractions. Once inside, the waiting times for rides were up to two hours each. To make matters worse, the most of the security check gates remained closed, further delaying entry. For the price paid, I expected much better crowd management and organization. What a shame for a park with so much potential.

I would like to express my deep dissatisfaction with my recent visit to Shanghai Disneyland. I traveled from another country specifically to visit this park, as it has long been my dream. Unfortunately, the experience turned out to be extremely disappointing. I arrived at the park at 8:30 AM and stayed until 4:30 PM. During these 8 hours, I was able to experience only 2 attractions. The waiting times were excessive: about 1.5 hours to enter the park and 2–3 hours for each attraction. On one occasion, I stood in line for 2.5 hours, only to be told at the end that the attraction had broken down and was unavailable. This was extremely frustrating, as the rides themselves last only a few minutes compared to hours of waiting. The overcrowding was overwhelming. Visitors were pushing, standing too close, and leaving litter on the ground. Today the temperature was 39°C with very high humidity, yet a large portion of the queues were outdoors, without proper shading or ventilation. Fans were extremely limited or absent. At one point, nearly half of the attractions were closed and unavailable for more than two hours. Additionally, the presence of Disney characters was very limited — they did not appear outdoors, and most seemed to remain inside buildings. The staff were mostly indoors under air conditioning, while guests were left waiting outside in the heat. Seating at dining areas was insufficient, and many tables were occupied by people resting or even sleeping after meals due to the lack of space. While the attractions themselves are of good quality, the overall guest experience was extremely unsatisfactory. Without VIP access, it is practically impossible to enjoy the park in a reasonable way. I respectfully request that my complaint be taken into consideration and that compensation be offered for the highly negative experience. Photos can be provided upon request.
Been there twice, recommend the fast ticket otherwise you will wait a long time for the rides. Great restaurant options and clean park!

Truly a Magical Experience at Shanghai Disneyland! Shanghai Disneyland is an absolute must-visit, offering a perfect blend of Disney magic with a modern twist. The TRON Lightcycle Power Run is an electrifying experience, racing through a neon-lit digital world at exhilarating speeds. The newly opened Zootopia brings the beloved city to life, complete with stunning details and immersive attractions. The Buzz Lightyear Planet Rescue ride is an upgrade from its counterparts, boasting advanced laser gameplay that will bring out your competitive spirit. For a delightful break, the English-speaking Mickey Mouse show is a heartwarming experience, especially for families with young children. As the day draws to a close, the fireworks and light show at the Enchanted Storybook Castle is simply breathtaking—Disney magic at its finest! Truly an unforgettable experience. ✨ 5/5 Stars ✨

Shanghai Disneyland is truly an extraordinary destination that everyone should experience at least once in their lifetime. Although I do not typically consider myself a fan of Disney-related attractions, the park’s unique charm and immersive atmosphere make it undeniably worthwhile. One aspect to be mindful of is the ticket price, which can be relatively expensive. However, the wide range of attractions, meticulously designed environments, and world-class entertainment justify the cost, making it a valuable investment for an unforgettable experience.The park also offers a diverse selection of culinary delights, with food vendors and restaurants serving both local and international cuisines. While the quality and variety are impressive, it is important to note that prices within the park are significantly higher than average. To manage expenses, I recommend bringing your own snacks and drinks to enjoy throughout the day. To make the most of your visit, I recommend arriving early, around 8:30 am. Additionally, be sure to download the official Shanghai Disneyland app beforehand. The app serves as an essential tool for navigation, ride wait times, show schedules, and other important information. Given the vast size of the park and the multitude of attractions, the app ensures that you remain organized and can make the most of your visit without unnecessary stress or confusion. In summary, Shanghai Disneyland offers a remarkable experience that transcends the typical theme park visit. With careful planning and preparation, you can fully immerse yourself in the magic while minimizing costs and maximizing enjoyment.

We had such a great time at Shanghai Disneyland! Managed to try out Zootopia: Hot Pursuit, Rex’s Racer, TRON Lightcycle Power Run (my personal favorite), Seven Dwarfs Mine Train and the Roaring Rapids water ride. Each attraction was unique and worth the expedited pass! We stayed all the way for the night fireworks, and it was absolutely spectacular! Overall, it was a magical experience with lots of fun rides, great atmosphere, beautiful souvenirs, and Disney charm all around. Definitely a must-visit if you’re in Shanghai!!
It's a fairytale land..I really enjoyed my time at Shanghai Disneyland. It brought out my inner child and reminded me how magical childhood feels.

Shanghai Disneyland was such a wonderful experience - definitely one of the best Disney parks we’ve ever visited. Compared to other Disneylands, it offers more variety and so many unique attractions that make it truly stand out. One highlight for me was Zootopia land - it’s such a one-of-a-kind addition, beautifully designed, and full of details that completely immerse you in the world. The other areas of the park are also outstanding (Harry Potter’s magical Hogsmeade, and of course Jurassic Park, Pirates of the Caribbean, Kung Fu Panda, and more.) The music, sights, and sounds throughout the park really draw you in and make you feel part of the story. On top of that, there are countless themed rides and magical touches everywhere you look. The food was also great! We highly recommend trying the turkey leg at the Tortuga Treats, and the Big Donut from Jumbeaux's Café! Overall, it was probably one of the best Disney experiences we’ve ever had, and I’d highly recommend it to anyone planning a trip to Shanghai!

Came on a Friday with a tour group. Was extremely crowded. The rides were worth queuing for as the effects were well done and the sets were built well. The food around the area was quite good as well. The soft ice cream was good, the big chicken leg was good. The Zootopia popsicle was hard so it’s ok to just get one. The food hall near the entrance was only decent. I would recommend getting the premier pass only for the popular rides such as TRON, Zootopia, Seven Dwarfs. You can also buy the single ride one-use which allows more control. It will save you a lot of time as waiting times can go up to 2 hours. Additionally, rides in the adventure area had high waiting times at the start but were significantly lower at the end of the day so you can go there after taking the popular rides. Only the experiential Jack Sparrow ride was worth it in that area. I also stayed for the fireworks at 9.15. People started queuing quite early so I only managed to get a spot at the entrance viewing the castle (I saw some gathering at 7.30 but it was cold so I only started queuing at 8.45). The fireworks were definitely pretty but if you want to see the projection on the castle more clearly then you should queuing closer to it much earlier.
A very memorable experience playing with toys and enjoying the projection mapping show at Shanghai Disneyland.

A Dream Come True at Shanghai Disneyland! 🌟 Visiting Shanghai Disneyland was truly like stepping into a dream. As someone who has loved Disney since childhood, this experience meant everything to me. I’ve memorized all the characters and never get tired of the magic Disney brings — and this park delivered it all in the most spectacular way! Every corner of Shanghai Disneyland is filled with wonder, from the enchanting castles to the joyful parades. But the TRON Lightcycle Power Run? Absolutely mind-blowing! It’s hands down the best ride I’ve ever been on — the speed, the lights, the thrill — I felt like I was racing through a futuristic world. It gave me goosebumps! I truly loved every single moment I spent there. The music, the rides, the food, the atmosphere — everything was perfect. It felt like my childhood dreams came alive right in front of me. My heart is set on visiting all the Disney parks around the world, and this visit only made that dream stronger. Shanghai Disneyland has set the bar so high, and I can’t wait to experience more of the magic in other places. Thank you Disney, for keeping the magic alive for all of us who never stopped believing! ✨🏰💫

Shanghai Disneyland (上海迪士尼乐园) was undoubtedly the highlight of our trip. We decided to enter the park after having lunch outside. We booked the entrance tickets via Klook. Thankfully, there was no queue at the entrance, and the entry process was smooth and quick. We just needed to scan our passport. Upon entering, we did a loop around the park to scout out the rides we wanted to take. Since my friend has a fear of heights, I went ahead solo to queue for the two most popular rides: the Seven Dwarfs Mine Train and TRON Lightcycle Power Run. The Seven Dwarfs Mine Train queue took around an hour, but I used the single rider lane, which definitely helped shorten the wait. The TRON ride, on the other hand, took about 1.5 hours to queue as there was no single rider option — only standard and priority access queues were available. Despite the long wait, both rides were absolutely worth it. We caught a street show that featured a great variety of Disney characters and dancers, which added a fun and festive vibe to the afternoon. But the true highlight — the crème de la crème — was the Nighttime Illumination Show at the castle. My friend managed to secure a prime viewing spot, and people had already started gathering by 6.00pm, even though the show only started at 9.15pm. The light, projection, and fireworks display was simply magical — comparable, if not better, than the shows we’ve seen at Tokyo and Hong Kong Disneyland. Definitely not one to miss! That said, exiting the park after the show was intense — the crowd was massive. However, the ushers were professional and well-trained, efficiently directing the flow of people and maintaining order to prevent any chaos or stampede. For families with young children, we strongly recommend either staying at the Disney Resort or leaving a bit later to avoid the crush of the crowd and ensure everyone's safety. Overall, it was a magical experience and a must-visit for anyone heading to Shanghai.
We went on December holiday where it was quiet crowded. We took a couple of fast passes to maximize the day

A magical place for kids and anyone who grew up loving Disney characters. The park is huge and beautifully designed, filled with so many details that make every corner feel like part of a story. The atmosphere is cheerful and exciting, especially during the parade and fireworks show in the evening — definitely a highlight worth staying for. It’s best to plan your visit in advance, as the park can get quite crowded. Downloading the Shanghai Disneyland app is a must — it helps you check real-time waiting times, locate attractions, and reserve entry for popular rides. Expect long queues for major attractions like TRON Lightcycle Power Run, Pirates of the Caribbean: Battle for the Sunken Treasure, and Soaring Over the Horizon, but the experiences are well worth the wait. Food options are varied, though slightly expensive, as you’d expect in a theme park. The staff are friendly and helpful, even if English communication can be limited. If you’re a Disney fan, this park won’t disappoint — it’s clean, well-managed, and full of that signature Disney magic. Just make sure to wear comfortable shoes, stay hydrated, and start early to make the most of your day.

Nice park not so crowded but some rides have a long waiting line up to 150 minutes (rides like Tron or Zootopia) the fireworks are amazing an everything looks as pretty as it looks on the website if not more . The subway station is a little far compre to other Disneylands but still on the close side you can enter with all the food and water you want and you are allowed to dress like the characters

Hands down one of the best Disneyland parks we’ve visited! The rides are incredible—thrilling, immersive, and perfect for all ages. Plus, the park is absolutely massive, with so much to explore. A truly magical experience from start to finish!
On October 20th, it was quite cold at 18°C. The queue wasn't very long that day, so I recommend everyone choose a weekday instead of a public holiday, weekend , for a shorter wait.

Visited on Christmas day as a surprise treat for my daughter and it could not have been better. We arrived around 7:10 am and decided there and then to upgrade our tickets to early entry. This allowed us to enter the park at 7:30 and 'beat the queues'. By 8:00 am we'd already been on the 7 Dwarves Mine Train and Tron Light Cycle ...three times ! She loved that ride so much. By 8:30 main gate was open and park was getting busier but not over crowded. Queues for most attractions were 30 to 40 minutes and we even managed Pirates of the Carribbean twice, that was a favourite - a technical marvel of sets, animatronics, sounds, smells and huge screens, plus a surprise reverse drop at the end. Disney being Disney, the attention to detail is phenomenal. Toy Story land may be for younger kids but the entire set and structural work is based on Tinkertoy, Meccano and other childhood memories. Even the lightbulbs used in different areas reflected the theme. My only negative was that some of the rides are just too short - worth queueing for 20 minutes but not longer. Well done Disney and Well done China !

Shanghai Disneyland feels very different from Tokyo Disneyland, more spacious, modern, and high-tech. Rides like TRON and Pirates of the Caribbean are unique, and the shows and parades are grand and immersive.

Beautiful park, way too many people. They should limit the passes or buy a fast pass. Monday 30th of June was expecting less people. But around 09:30 more than 1 hour to enter in extreme hot weather. Tron, 1.5 hour wait again huge line in the extreme sun. Pirate of the Caribbean beautiful show! More than 1 hour waiting but it felt more like Turkish steambath before entering! Would not recommend to go in the summer months or only early or late hours.
Great food, loved the pirates of the carribean ride, clean toilets with AC, crowds are alot but the lines go quick to get to rides.

One of the must go place when u visiting Shanghai with your family. You should go there at least 2 days so u can spend the time for parade and also firework at night. Must visit zootopia special at Shanghai.

Excellent disney park (once you get through the parking lot of local sales people. I think the lot is public property since they are not beyond the escalator to the bridge which security keeps them out of). A couple words of advice (since Google isn't allowed to work in China wifi), if you know you want to ride ALOT of rides either just buy the premier pass for the big rides in a bundle (saves you money to prepay for which ones you want versus buy them separately), or wait till later at night when ride times dramatically drop. For the parade we had a great viewing spot infront of mickey and pals cafe without any issues. For fireworks unless you literally want to sit front row castle (which they still seat you in lines so someone may sit infront of you) then you can buy the premium firework viewing (west entrance is just past Dumbo on the left) Overall most cast members speak english or pick up basic sign language when you point to something like when we had to buy socks. I definitely recommend visiting at least 2-3 days as there are a LOT of cool shows (dont miss the rhythm show and captain Jack's stunt adventure). We stayed at the Hilton science center, a luxury didi (china's uber) was 10$ or less everyday.

Shanghai Disneyland is a stunning fusion of high-tech marvels and seasonal charm. Visiting just before Christmas offers a unique "Winter Frostival" atmosphere, though the heavy crowds are a significant factor to manage. The Pros * Immersive Zootopia: The new Zootopia land is a masterpiece of detail; Hot Pursuit is a must-ride despite the wait. * Holiday Atmosphere: The "snowfall" on Mickey Avenue and the seasonal castle projections are breathtakingly festive. * Top-Tier Tech: TRON and Pirates of the Caribbean remain the most advanced Disney attractions globally. The Cons (The 4-Star Trade-off) * Massive Queues: Pre-Christmas crowds saw wait times for headliners soaring past 150 minutes. * Winter Chill: Standing in long outdoor lines in near-freezing temperatures is taxing. * Congestion: Navigating the main thoroughfares during parades and fireworks can feel overwhelming. Verdict It is a world-class park that truly shines during the holidays, but the pre-Christmas rush is intense. To make the most of it, Disney Premier Access is highly recommended to bypass the heavy holiday lines. Would you like me to look up the current prices for Disney Premier Access to help you budget for a future visit?

A version of Disneyland for Chinese people and open for all ,! Affordable ticket price. Worth to visit when in Shanghai. Please book your ticket in advance and if you need halal food, please make a reservation 3 days before arrival using Disneyland Shanghai apps.

Amazing park but very overcrowded. Expect to wait at least for 60 minutes for any ride. Some ride had a waiting time of 180 minutes. If you can get the priority pass it is very wirth it. The parades were amazing so was the illumination show at 20:00. Food and drink processions are inflated but it is to be expected. All in all a very cool experience and definitely worth a visit.

Had a wonderful time at Shanghai Disneyland! The ticket seller was friendly, and the park wasn’t too crowded—especially on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday when tickets are also a bit cheaper. The park is absolutely beautiful and well-maintained. While the staff were kind and helpful, communication in English was limited, so it’s helpful to have a translation app on hand. The nighttime fireworks show was truly magical and a highlight of the visit! We also enjoyed the restaurants in Disneytown—lots of good food options and a nice atmosphere. Overall, a great experience and definitely worth a visit! Zootopia land was the highlight
Absolutely love the perks of staying at the Disneyland Hotel, you get to enter the park earlier then no waiting for most of the rides for the first hour.

Amazing park but rating two stars for the terrible app experience. Doesn’t work well with international phones or numbers, we brought a package that included coupons and we’ve wasted over an hour trying to use them. Should be far simpler than this, every other park around the world we’ve been to have apps that load and work fast and smoothly, by far the worst app experience. Plus 90% of food seems to have to be ordered through the app and it makes the experience frustrating.

One day is not enough, best game ever is the soaring over the horizon as a Perfect experince, also try pirates of the caribbean battle 4 sunken treasure you will dive in the sea "logically" I love the day

It's a good theme park to explore, just that the timing to wait for a ride during peak season may not be pleasant for the kids. Weather is cool, food wise mostly western style, do not expect Mala Chicken Chop in there, standard of food is borderline.

Visiting **Shanghai Disneyland** during Christmas week is magical. The entire park is transformed into a winter wonderland with **Christmas trees**, **lights**, and **festive music** The cobblestone streets of Disney Town are especially enchanting, twinkling with Christmas lights and decors! There are **holiday-themed parades**, **live performances**, and **holiday treats** available. You can enjoy **Christmas carols** and even find some Disney characters dressed in festive outfits. Crowds and Wait Times While Christmas week can be busy, it's generally less crowded than other peak times like Chinese New Year. If you plan your visit well, you can avoid long lines and enjoy the attractions more comfortably. Buying express pass early is cheaper too. December in Shanghai can be cold, so be sure to dress warmly and bring layers. The cooler weather can make the outdoor activities more enjoyable. Our overall experience and findings the atmosphere during Christmas week to be incredibly festive and joyful. It's a great time to experience the magic of Disney with a holiday twist.

Once in a life time, recommend. Rainy day wasn’t always a bad day. There was less crowded. Fast queue and short waiting time, love it 😍. We enjoyed the Top 3 rides twice in a roll. Rain was gone right after afternoon, so we had fun with Parade and fireworks. 😀😀😀😀

What an absolutely MAGICAL experience! Absolutely LOVED Shanghai Disneyland ♥️ If you're wondering if the Premier Access package is worth it, it 1,000% is. As someone who's been to Disneyland with both, the pleb ticket and the premier access one, I'll never go back to the normal ticket. You spend 90-120 minutes in a queue for a 30 second ride, wasting an entire day in hot weather, in queues... This may be fine for a small Disneyland like Hong Kong's, but anything bigger than the Paris one - you won't cover the entire park in one day on a normal ticket, not to mention how shitty you'll be by the end of it. There are people EVERYWHERE, it's hot, and you're just waiting in queues, ALL. DAY. The Premier Access package with the hotel is so worth the money. It includes a night at their hotel, dinner at Aurora restaurant, breakfast, lunch, 13 x fast pass rides (trust me, this is enough), early entry to the park, digital photo pass and surprise freebies. Just save the extra money if you go to Disneyland. It's something like AU$1,660 each (each for 2 people, so AU$3,300 in total), and definitely worth it. 💯

Sanghai Disneyland was the first ever Disneyland I ever went too and it didn't disappoint at all! The lines were long to get inside but after we got in we just didn't want to go out at all! The place is so big that I actually got tired from all the walking at the end of the day. Unfortunately I didn't get to ride on Tron as it was under maintenance when I went there but I did get to ride the pirates of Carribbean, the seven dwarfs mine coaster, Disney castle experience from inside, the ferry experience. The caramel popcorn was delicious here too! I wish we had more time to try more rides here. Even though I didn't understand Chinese I was getting the full Disney experience here! 10/10 would recommend people to visit this Disneyland at least once and especially try out the pirates in the Carribbean!!

Overall a good experience. The park is big but not as massive as some Florida theme parks. We got there at 930am on Christmas morning which was a Thursday (not a national Chinese Holiday). Most guests are college kids with friends or on dates. It took about 15-20 minuted to get through security and the park entrance. Must bring your passport for everything in China. I would also 100% recommend getting the fast pass. There were 3, 6, 12 ride fast pass options about 60/120/230$ for those tiers. We got a 6 ride option. My kids are 5 and 7. My dad was able to add a fast pass for us from his hotel room while we were walking around but I think going to guest services they can add one for you. It gets added to your admissions ticket and you scan it at the fast pass entrances (and once again right before the ride to deter people to jump lines). If you are more adept with WeChat I think you can even scan the ride QR code at the ride entrance and add each ride for about 20$ à la carte. The Disney app was helpful to get around the park but I couldn’t figure out how to add additional fast passes there. Fast pass shortened most rides from 1 hour down to 2-10 minutes. We did the 6 ride package which had Zootopia, Pirates, Soaring, Dumbo, buzz Lightyear, and Ariel. The only other 3 rides I saw that would have been good to add to ours are: Tron, Winnie the Pooh, and Mine Cart (7 Dwarves) Importantly, the fast pass we got allowed us to skip the line just to get into the zootopia part of the park, which was a 60 minute wait without the fast pass. zootopia is very popular in China. I think it was because the zootopia ride was part of my fast pass package. I would check with the website or guest service staff if this is a priority for you. The food options in Pinocchio’s Tavern were all pretty good (egg noodle with braised beef, fried rice and turkey leg). There are other food options throughout the park and they all looked good. You can rent strollers outside the park for about 50$ for a double and then 9$ if you want the blanket (can keep). This allowed my jet lagged kids to nap throughout the park and I would definitely recommend. It. We didn’t make it to night time or fireworks but I hear it’s beautiful. Overall my kids had a blast. It was 45 degrees in 90% humidity which felt like 35 degrees. Summer temps will feel hotter than the numerical temp if you go in the summer due to humidity.

As the tagline says it is the happiest place on earth. It was a great weather when I visited. It was cold with a warm sun. Download the app to see the waiting time of the rides. It was so accurate and we just plan accordingly based on the waiting time. Great night time show, second one preferably since it was that crowded anymore. Came two days in a row. Finished most of the rides within two days. Came early for the first day and a lot of people was rushing to enter the park.

My family had a round folding chair that we were going to bring along but we weren't allowed to bring it into the park. Everyone, please take note to avoid having to carry it around. Disneyland has very strict security at the entrance so you will see a long line, but the plus point is that you can bring your own snacks without being banned. Regarding the games, I think the Pirates of the Caribbean game is the most underrated, it's very beautiful and grand but the waiting time is only 15 minutes. On the contrary, the hot game, the 7 Dwarfs, has almost no plot, just a very fast train ride. Overall, Food in the park is good.

We had an unforgettable day at Shanghai Disneyland! Getting there was very easy — we used DiDi (China’s version of Uber) from downtown Shanghai, and it took about 40–50 minutes depending on traffic. Super convenient and affordable, especially if you’re traveling as a group. Be prepared: the crowds start forming before the park even opens! We arrived around 7:30 AM and there was already a long line at the entrance. Definitely buy your tickets in advance and arrive early if you want to make the most of your day. What makes Shanghai Disneyland unique compared to other Disney parks (like in Tokyo or California) is its exclusive attractions. Don’t miss: • TRON Lightcycle Power Run – futuristic, high-speed coaster you won’t find in any other Disneyland. • Pirates of the Caribbean: Battle for the Sunken Treasure – a mind-blowing ride with next-level technology and massive sets. Nothing like the original versions! • Camp Discovery and Roaring Rapids offer a fun, adventurous break from the usual Disney feel. The castle here is also the biggest Disney castle in the world, beautifully designed and stunning at night. While it gets extremely crowded, especially on weekends and holidays, the experience is still magical if you plan well. Use the app to manage wait times, and consider purchasing a Premier Access pass for popular rides. Clean, well-maintained, with friendly staff and lots of food options. A must-visit if you’re in Shanghai!

Expect long queues and long waiting time for the rides if you are not purchasing the fast pass. This place is great. However some NO BRAIN adults are SMOKING inside even there are children around. The staffs are closing their eyes eventho we already inform them. Disneyland management please improve on this!!!

Shanghai Disneyland is absolutely a wonderful place that is full of magic! I've been to the ones in Hong Kong SAR, Tokyo and Paris. Those parks are way too small and lack of interesting attractions especially Paris, maybe half the size of Shanghai one? The Zootopia section is a must for your visit which is exclusive to this Disneyland. Staff are friendly and helpful, they helped us to seek help when we did not know how to speak Chinese. The park is full of technological stuff, Tomorrow Land is a perfect example, the Tron ride was excellent! We went for the firework at 10pm so as to skip the crowd at 9pm(there are two timing for fireworks --9and 10) don't miss the firework as i think just by watching it, you'd have earned back half the ticket price! The food here not so cheap but have some local flavours,. Deserts and drinks are quite good. (idk what are the reviews complaining about the customer service, they served us nice. If you've been to the Disneyland in Florida, you would know what a bad customer service mean) Really try Shanghai Disney, you'll be so amazed!!

It was fine. We spent two days here and didn't see everything possible. My 7 year old daughter loves the Zootopia area the most. However, the queue for the Hot Pursuit is, on average, 40 minutes each time. We spent most of our time here. On top of that, there is a queue to enter the Zootopia area. At least 40 minutes as well. There aren't many food options in the Zootopia area, so either eat ahead of time or bring some food with you. In the main Disneyland Park everything is extremely pricey. Food, fast passes, souvenirs, etc. It's all expensive. The queues for the rides are ridiculously long. We went on a weekend while school was still in session in the country. I couldn't imagine the weekends or weekends in the Summer months. Overall, I would not come back. Once is too many times.

My childhood memories came alive here. I'm not a fan of the rides and the theme park. But the fact that I was there in a place that made my childhood better was enough for me. I saw the waiting for rides or shows were about 30 to 45 minutes (this was on a weekday ya). But I did not go for all that. If I had a child, I would have joined, but I was alone so yup skipped it all and enjoyed the nostalgia. Great for children. Great to get your childhood memories realised (for those above 40yo ya 😉). Had a great time.

We visited the Park on a Monday thinking we wouldn’t need to queue up for long as it is weekday however the shortest queue was 45 minutes, many attractions had 90 minutes wait time and the wait time for character encounters was 270-300 minutes! This is not normal! I have been to Hong Kong Disneyland and Paris Disneyland, their lines were much shorter. It is not fun when you wait 1.5 hour for a 50 seconds ride! To fix this issue and make the experience actually enjoyable, the maximum number of visitors that the park can admit needs to be reduced.

Tiring but exciting and entertaining at the same time. Disneyland Shanghai offers thrilling rides and immersive attractions, bringing Disney's magic to life in a modern, vibrant setting. With stunning parades, shows, and unique themed lands, it's a fun-filled adventure for all ages.

Was fun, very different to the other Disney around the world, but we enjoyed it a lot.... Less about running to the fastest ride .. it was more about being there and enjoy. Definitely Asians prefer Zootopia characters over Mikey;-)

I went to disney on a super crowned day (70min+ walk and wait to be able to go inside) but all the progress go smoothly after that so it was a nice trip for me (I recommend buying fast pass for a better experience if you budget wasn't too tight)
It was a tiring but magical day for us at Disneyland. Do research more on the Disney premier excess, pay a little more to skip the long ques for the very popular rides!

I booked the ticket online the night before, and I was able to easily pay with a foreign (non-Chinese) travel card. The tickets were then linked to my passports, so it is very important to remember to take your passport with you as this is now your entry ticket. I visited on a weekday in mid February, and arrived just before opening time. Entry was quick and easy (including bag inspections). A lot of the rides were walk-on with minimal wait times during the morning. It became a bit busier in the afternoon, but was still very manageable. The Park was beautiful, clean and easy to navigate. That was amazing. First time been there, it was a great experience. Despite the weather, it was also a good time spent there alone, watching people having fun and lots of characters from Disney world. The most memorable was you can line up to take photos with them and have conversations with them as well. My ticket included a free meal and drink, which was great value. I chose spaghetti and meatballs, which was huge and filled me up for the day. The menu prices seemed quite reasonable, especially for a Disney park. I bought the PhotoPass, and had some issues trying to get it to work/download, but the staff in the photo shop were amazingly patient and helpful in getting it to finally work. It was a magical place, it makes you feel like a kid again, no matter how old you are. I loved it. I was disappointed to discover Pirates of the Caribbean was closed, but it's a great excuse to revisit in the future!
The park is huge, clean, and beautifully designed, with incredible attention to detail.

The experience was better than expected (grew up with Disney). Went with 2 year old. This was on the 26th December. Crowd wasn't huge. Waiting times at rides 30-80 mins. We managed to go in 4 rides with our 2-year-old and 2 additional for adults. We visited 3 areas in detail and 2 we just passed through. Positive: - great staff (except at the Mickey memory house: we had a gift card for a photo shoot that we got from friends who visited 2 weeks before. The staff did not even scan it, but claimed it was probably fake anyway and that it was too late for a shoot anyway at 19:30h. Very rude!) - clean - Picknick area with warm tents - entry / exit logistic very well organized!!! After fireworks at closing there was no feeling of "panic: too many people leaving at the same time!" - public transport connections - whole park has guest wifi (enable reception of roaming sms for the login code) Negative: - no Star Wars area - no favorite characters roaming the park to meet. Only at specific times at specific places. A park as this should have at least 10 of each famous character walk around for ppl to take photos with or at least the little ones to slave at - Restaurants have no physical menus, but only through QR scan. That's not ok. - waiting lines can be insane and skip-the-line tickets are very expensive

Must visit while in Shanghai! We got our tickets from Klook which was cheaper and very easy to link to the Disneyland app. We got the early entry pass on the app as well which I think is really worth it as we saved a lot of time. We managed to take three popular rides in that one hour. The more famous rides were Tron, Zootopia, Pirates of the Caribbean and some photo ops with Lina Bell. I think the food options in park is affordable and tasted nice and decent portion unlike what many mentioned, but the downside is it’s hard to find seats. We had to stand at some corner to eat our bowl of seafood rice haha. Also please try the big turkey leg as it’s so good esp during cold weather. There are parades throughout the day and there’s fireworks too which we skipped as we wanted to avoid the crowd. There are a lot more restaurants in Disney town which is a free area to explore and you can re enter to Disneyland afterwards.

Not the happiest place on Earth as Walt Disney like this to be. Long wait and unfriendly cast members. It seems like the employees are stressed and unhappy. The trend is similar across different rides. Second hand smokes everywhere. Smokers light up almost any where they like. A lot of parents pushing big trollies. At the Eye of the storm show, the locals rush and run. The staff have to remind the audience to walk. Illegal touts peddling rain coat, umbrella and hats. Not a great experience. The saving grace is the effort they put into the Tron rides (30 sec - 1 min)

Came on a weekday and the queue wasn’t that bad compared to the one in Japan. Would advise to buy tickets in advance before coming, redemption was easy and tickets were printed on the spot, just show them your booking QR code. Queues are manageable and didn’t really needed to buy the express pass. There’s a Disney village right outside the park and there were lots of food options! Also, the tron theme was incredibly well done! We will return to shanghai Disney land again.

Absolutely magical! I have been to other Disneyland parks before but this one had some cool rides that are not there in other parks. Like the tron! And the camp discovery trails. Loved being here. Although, visiting in summers is extremely hard here. Super duper hot. But the park was still fully packed. Woudl recommend buying the early access to ticket to beat the queues and the heat. Almost no one speaks English at the park. But there is WiFi. And the Disney Shanghai app works fine. Plenty of restaurants to eat at. Veg food can be challenging but Winnie the Pooh had veg pizza. And there are many kiosks selling icecream coconut water etc. The illuminate show is out of this world and I cannot recommend riding the tron enough.

So so easily accessible! So close to Shanghai Pudong International Airport! Took us one hour, direct train, from Courtyard by Marriot Hotel, Shanghai!! We were the 7.30am early bird entries!! Excitement was already in the air on the train! So crazy to see these well dressed up bubbly youths rushing through the gates to the entrance! Disney world Shanghai is a massive park with so many many rides to choose from! The smart young kids would start from the most popular rides first before the general crowds swamp in!! The online entry ticket came with food vouchers! Not bad at all! Everything is so new and fresh, the gardens immaculate, visitors dressing their parts…. All very orderly and neat! Long queues can be seen as the day progresses…. We were there from 7.30am till 10pm, still not enough!! We would soon return!! Feel safe, orderly, easily accessible by public transport, the whole place was well staffed with helpful people! There is even a medical centre in there !

Wonderful place to be....the rides are for all group ages and they ate free once you pay for the entry ticket...and the toy shops and candy shops are worth a visit but everything is too pricey if you're a foreigner and your currency is different. It's a big place and there is so much to do and see so reach there as soon as it opens so you can make the best of your visit. Also there was hours of wait for each ride even on a working day...that makes the experience tiring. The parade in the evening and the light and fireworks show at 8:00p.m night ate worth seeing.. so amazing. It's a lifetime experience to visit disney.

It’s so bad !! The crowd is too much . The que and the walking is crazy . From the gate where you get dropped off till you enter the Disney park is enough to make you exhausted. The crowds are uncontrolled , the humidity and the amount of walking just to enter the park is ridiculous. Time to wait for each ride is almost 2 hours . The toilet are extremely dirty and disgusting . There is no much options for food either and if there is , then there is no place to sit . Never going again

The place is magical yes. But the waiting time for each ride or entertainment is horrible. There is hardly any public seating in the park and crowd management is very poor. Each show is not worth having to wait for 50 to 60 minutes as it lasts for only around 10 minutes. It doesn’t have all the characters but shopping at the stores is really good and prices are compatible cheaper to the other disnleyland locations that I have been to. Please purchase your tickets in advance and opt for premium aces or gravely reduces waiting time and queues even the early bird access is amazing

Queue for popular rides are over 90 mins and can go as high as 150 mins for peak days. Be prepared to pay for premier access at any CNY$180 per ride if you want to speed queue. Park is big and there is Zootopia, which is most popular now after the movie.

Visited Shanghai Disneyland for whole day in early Dec. Since we staying at Toy Story hotel. Hotel guest have privilege to enter 1hr early compared to official park opening. Take shuttle bus from Toy Story hotel to park. Tickets were bought in advance. No issue to bring cup noodles. Tripod stand & selfie stick was not allowed. Crowd are mainly locals & minimal overseas tourist. Multiple rides are kids friendly There are plenty of shops, but there’s no halal friendly stall or foods. There are no halal foods in Disney town either. Muslim travellers will need to bring alternative halal foods or need to exit Disney land area. And take taxi 10mins away for halal restaurant. No issue to exit & re-enter. Fireworks at 2015HR.
The Disneyland tour was very impressive. All rides were cute and safe. Both adults and children can play. There was a parade in the evening and we could see fireworks and lights at night.

Disneyland is so magical but the crowded is real even weekdays also people mountain people sea. Waiting time for each ride or entertainment is horrible and each show is only last for around 10 minutes. If can afford, prefer to purchase Disney Dream Day Package (including Disney Premier Access) in advance, can reduce waiting time and queues. Last but not least, we feel that Disney Dream Day Package is very worth it!

The Disney theme was the only thing attractive. Most rides are very basic, very mild thrill levels. There are wayyyyyy too many people. We went there on a weekday and most rides wait times are 90 to 120 mins. Can't imagine what it would be on weekends. Impossible to go on the rides we want. We had to give up our favourite rides. To give some examples, the carrousel wait time is 40 mins. The seven dwarf 120 mins. Over the horizon 105 mins. The doggy ride was the longest we waited for. 40 mins in the line and the ride spinned for one minute. Seriously a waste of time. We stayed in the park for ten hours and only played six rides. Not worth the time. Young kids would be exhausted so not recommended.

I highly recommend purchasing the Premier Access Adventure Set of 6 tickets when visiting Shanghai Disneyland. This set grants you access to some of the park’s must-see rides, including Tron Lightcycle Power Run, Zootopia, Seven Dwarfs Mine Train, and Pirates of the Caribbean. These attractions are truly exceptional and definitely worth the experience, especially with the convenience of Premier Access. It allows you to skip the long lines and make the most of your time in the park!

We bought the ticket 1 month in advance and early entering pass. Queued for 30 mins as we reached before 730am. It took awhile to enter due to the security bag check and passport scan. We went during the non peak time, considering no need to queue too long for some of the famous rides like Zootopia straight to the front and enter the car, Pirate of the Caribbean waited 10 mins and etc. No full water bottle allow, you can bring empty bottle to fill the water inside the park. But the water tasted rusty, for baby I think better to purchase the mineral water. Plenty of toilet around the theme park, very clean too. Restaurant food okok la, high price and not nice. You may opt to go out of the theme park to eat, and re-entering again. Fireworks just very ordinary to me.. but all in all, it's a very nice experience due to the cooling weather.

Wow, this is a beautiful park. We came from Australia and can't speak a work of the local languages, but that did not matter at all. The park is well maintained and clean, and the rides are out of this world. Well worth investing in an early entry ticket to avoid the long lines.

Our visit to Shanghai Disneyland was magical but required some planning. It’s essential to buy tickets in advance as the park is very crowded every day. Even on a weekday, it took us 2 hours to enter due to the long lines. Despite the crowds, the park's attractions, parades, and shows were absolutely worth it. The attention to detail and the immersive environments in each themed land are impressive. The character interactions and entertainment were top-notch, making it a delightful experience for both kids and adults. Be sure to arrive early, plan your day, and take advantage of FastPass to make the most of your visit. Overall, a must-visit for Disney fans, but be prepared for the crowds and long waits.

The happiest place on earth but expect everything to be Chinese. Lines were not long since we went on a weekday but everything was lovely. There was nice weather, the food was good and you can feel the happiness all around the place.

Had a great time, even though I couldnt understand 95% of all performances and rides.. it was all in Chinese xD its worth the visit for the zootopia area, since its the only one :) overall great experience and staff were all friendly
Worst Disneyland visited, please return my childhood dream. No crowd control, over commercialized..

It was okay, but there was too many people in one place, if you don’t want to spend extra money you have to wait in one or more hours to get to do something, so you basically waste more time on waiting than playing and enjoying the park, it also takes a lot of time to even get into the park. But otherwise all the things we did were really fun, I recommend the seven dwarves train or whatever it was called, 😅, the parade was also entertaining.

A great Disney theme park. Huge space, plenty of rides and attractions, one whole day of fun. It is a must visit place while you in Shanghai. Just note that in August it getd very busy and crowded due to school holidays, which prolong wsiting time for some rides/attractions up to 1 or 2 hours, long lines. August also hot month, with strong sun, this makes some attractions difficult to attend especially with long waiting time. The best time to visit is September, weather so perfect, less crowds, can make it unforgettable visit. I must recommend Pirates of the Carribean ride, it is THE BEST, although the dialoge in Chinese, still enjoyable. See the videos. Another recommended ride is the 3D Flight, must have one, I waited 60 min in line to get this ride. The closing show is a must see. I can not describe how azing it is, just watch the videos posted with this review and you will get the picture. The park also has several shops where you can buy a lot of Disney-themed goods for all ages. It is best to purchase the tickets in advanced if you visit during school holidays 10/10 must visit

Beautiful and distinct Disney park. There are many little touches that are great, but there are also a lot of rides too dependent on projections. There is also far too much attention given to the recent live action remakes over the original content. Zootopia land is pretty great!

If you do not have express pass, nothing magical about this place, 2-3 hours waiting for popular facilities. FYI, You can upgrade to express pass for each single facility on their app after enter the park.

Must visit if you are in Shanghai! Easier if you buy your ticket in advance and do plan your itinerary beforehand because it gets crowded regardless of weekend or weekdays or holiday season. Don’t hesitate to try all kinds of food and buy souvenirs because u don’t go to Disneyland to save money. (and good luck on your travel bc i know not having much information on google is a bit frustrating!) ⭐️ and another tips is do come early to get to try as many attractions as u can and some rides like tron/zootopia are worth the DPA! 🐭
Nice place to visit especially those with children. Easy to reach by public transport or taxis

I arrived about 45 minutes after opening time, on a cloudy/rainy Thursday in October, with a general ticket (no priority), and managed to see over ten of the attractions before closing time. The queuing time was quite long as to be expected, sometimes over an hour, but I utilised the single rider option when available to minimise that. Also consider the rides only last about five minutes each. I also bought my own snacks to avoid time eating lunch. They did confiscate my selfie stick though. Overall I was happy that I was able to see more than I expected.

reviews.authorName: 皎月君 เจี่ยวเยว่จวิน
reviews.text: Buying the tickets early can be time-saving. And it takes only your passport to get in. Trust me, get there as early as possible. However, even when we went there on Monday, the lines were still long. It was quite crowded. Rides that you shouldn’t miss are Zootopia and Tron bicycles. Besides, you don’t want to miss the last illumination show at 9:15. It’s really worth the wait. The birthday badge gets you nothing but a lot of wishes from their staff.

Had fun time in Disneyland! We went on Monday and Tuesday. Got our tickets on Trip.com early bird tickets for 5 at 600+ for 2 days! Did not purchase any Premier access pass & was glad we did not. Cause we managed to get on all rides which the kids like. Did zootopia x 3, Tron x 5, buzz lightyear x 2, Seven Dwarf train ride x1, Soaring the High x 1, took pic with Mickey, Interacted with Judy & Nic, watched parade, watched fireworks, basically did all that the kids wanted to. Had a happy time. ❤️
