I was very impressed with the Shanghai Disneyland Park, and my family had a great time there. Highlights for me were the Tron, the Rapids, and Pirates of the Caribbean rides, which we all absolutely loved. The parades and fireworks at the end of the day were also fabulous. For our older kids, I felt there weren't as many big rides as the Paris resort, but there was plenty to see and do. We visited on a Friday, and I had a lot of anxiety about our pre-purchased tickets and getting entry to the park. However, it turned out to be quite a smooth process, and I wouldn't have been concerned if the communication was better. Although I had the tickets on the park app, they only seemed to need my passport number to see our tickets. FYI you need to bring your physical passport with you. You definitely need to have the app downloaded; as well as providing a map of the Park with your GPS location, it provides information on all the ride status's and times which is really useful. It also has a timetable of all the events, but the timings were definitely off, so we missed the start of the parade. The park was busier than I expected for an off-peak week day in October, but queue times were acceptable. We queued for about an hour for big rides like Tron, but got very lucky with some of the other rides, queuing for maybe 30 minutes or less. A couple of rides had queue times exceeding 2 hours for the entire day, so we chose not to queue for them. The food at the park is expensive, and you'll need WeChat or Ali Pay to purchase them in most cases. I think I only used cash for smaller purchases like drinks and ice creams. The toilets are well maintained and clean, but as a warning, they use a lot of the "squat toilets" on the ground, which was interesting... When we visited, there were a lot of "influencers" there. They are dressed in costumes, normally a Disney princess, and have photographers following them around. They are literally everywhere, but they do highlight some good photo opportunities. They also don't seem to go on the rides! Leaving the park, you may be wise to leave at least 30-60 minutes before the park closes. Everyone will suddenly leave at once, and the volume of people is staggering. We decided to get a taxi back to the hotel because it was so busy, and it was surprisingly efficient and fast to do so. Google translate and a card for your hotel address is advisable, as none of them spoke English. I would definitely visit again.

Very good experience. Though the other Disney lands are better, we still had a very good experience here. The rides are good and dies not have much long queues. Food selection is good, would recommend this place.
My mistake was traveling on an important holiday in China — it was extremely crowded. I will definitely go to Disneyland again, but in another country

This is an extraordinary place in Shanghai where you should visit unavoidably. Yes I've never been bored to be like childhood again. What's the most exciting Play theme I advise you? TRON. What's the most fantastic Play theme I suggest you? Pirate of the Caribbean. What's the most fun play theme I convince you? Zootopia. And other themes you should play by yourself but don't forget to watch their last show on 2000 pm. too I kindly whisper. Ps. Don't think too much about Chinese toilets because they're cleaner than you believe even though there are more tourists over there. Unless cigarette smoke is bad smelling for me.

Having visited all the Disney parks in the world (yes every single one), i’ve found that the cast members here were not as enthusiastic and in-theme as compared to the others. I had expected the park to be bigger too, but it was a comfortable size and could be easily finished in a day. If you want to ride the popular rides without having to queue too long, i’d strongly recommend getting the Early Park Entry ticket. The early entry allows you to enjoy the park 1 hour before opening, and i managed to complete 4 rides (Tron, Zootopia, Pirates, Rex Racer) as well as take some really nice pictures without many photobombs. There are some park exclusive merchandise which you have to ballot for an entry to the shop to buy, so do install their disneyland app. Its also really useful to check wait times, show times and menus. Zootopia land is too cute to miss and for disney fans, please please please ride the pirates of the carribean! Its the best version out of all the other parks.

I went here for my 30th birthday and was a bit sad and disappointed. What you expect when you go to a Disney park is warmth and friendliness and an overall magical experience. Everyone was quite rude, they push and the staff don’t smile or greet you unless you’re going into the store. GETTING IN: You have to walk at least 30mins from the carpark and wait in line for at least an hour + before getting scanned in by security. (Photo below) WEATHER: For the heat it was hard, they didn’t have many fans or misters, there was no where to cool off but inside the stores and restaurants. People were sitting in the toilet blocks to cool off. There aren’t many options for cold drinks or ice cream. WAIT TIMES: Expect wait times of at least 120 min without a fast track pass. There isn’t much ride selection either. PARK APP: You need a Chinese phone number to be able to get fast track passes or sign into the app. We couldn’t do anything without it..
This is the first Disneyland I have ever visit. Great experience. Nice, fun and clean.

The Tron ride was amazing and worth the money. We came in Nov and weather was pretty chilly. The walk from carpark to the Disneyland entrance was pretty far though and a lot of unnecessary windy queues to go through. Overall still a 5 star for me.

We had pre purchased tickets as they sell out and we still had to line up even before security line up and then ticket checking prior to entry into the park. You need internet access to be able to find everything in the park on their app and also to purchase premier access to the popular rides which can have a queue of 2 hrs+... My internet crashed half way through so was unable to purchase the premier passes, completely frustrating. I have done all the Disney parks in the world and this one has by far THE best Pirates of the Caribbean ride out of all of them, no expense was spared and was well worth the wait in line. Highly recommend the Pirate stunt showas well. Way too many people even though it was a week day but was to be expected considering the population

Very nice Disney land, it is huge, a lot of games. Good for families and kids. The restaurants are limited (especially for foreigners) Many ice cream shops Also there are many gift shops In general, I would come again. But you need to prepare yourself and your family for a long, exhausted day. There's some hotels I think if you want to stay more than a day, The good thing is that the airport is located (20-30 min) from Disney Land Park. Highly recommend 👌

Zootopia and Pirates is top class. Also the Soar ride is unique experience . But that’s all. Long queues even 180 minutes , most rides remind local amusement parks in Balkans and the most rude staff ever . No Disney vibe but personnel with military mindset . No one speaks a single world of English and they do not even know how to use VISA payments. “Chinese style” disneyland . That says all
Very crowded. Expensive food and beverages. The rides are fun and some are really exciting!!! Good to spend an entire day. Magical if you grew up with Mickey and Donald!!!

Wonderful experience. Shorter queue compare to all other disneyland. Probably due to China has not started school holiday yet. The food in the park was okay... You probably get better food at the shopping area. Where u need to reenter the park subsequently.

Visited on 26/9/25 for celebrate birthday some staff is good day HBD to me and fireworks sound of music at castle is perfect but for male staff at tron and cashier at secret shop they not deserve to stay at amusement park as they behavior not good to me it so bad

Some of the best rides in all Disneylands! The Pirates of the Caribbean, Soaring, and Zootopia were my favourite. Zootopia is the new trackless ride which added some element of uncertainty and surprise. Food is not really good tho. Looks cute, well presented but expensive and not tasty. The only Disneyland in the world that allows patrons to bring own food. But there are rules on what type of food can be brought in. I’d still buy in Disney to save time. 95% of staff were friendly and helpful. I did meet 1 rude staff at Doug/Russell meet & greet. But most staff were very nice. I bought an extra early entry pass which really helped to beat the queue. Overall SHDL is worth visiting at least once!

pretty big, many rides for children and some suitable for adults. i enjoyed the pirates of the carribean rides very much. zootopia land was really cool and the ride was very fun too. the food was pretty varied and well priced. queues werent tooo bad but it was a tuesday afternoon in october so keep that in mind.

Should include more options for food intolerants, be careful with local food if you are a foreigner for even the "princess soups" are spicy. Coffe was awful everywhere. Bring an offline traductor along, it will help you a lot. The park is certainly small so you should complete it within a day. Use fast pass only for very specific atractions, not that good for multiple.

Highly recommend to buy tickets in advance and bring your IDs with you to retrieve your tickets at entrance. We arrived on a rainy weekday so there were not many people and all the rides required 10 minutes or less waiting time. All the rides and shows were delivered in Mandarin (Putonghua). We did not dine inside but most food items were quite expensive and not really that attractive. Free water machines are available across the park.

The best disneyland park ever in the world! The park is huge for 1 park only, and a good combination of the old and new type of rides. The zootopia land is so niceeee… also dont miss the Illuminate show at night, it is definitely one of the best!!

Beautiful place for kids and families. Very hot in August. Has water falls and many other amusement places for kids and families. There is even a small shopping area. Prices om higher side. BIG BIG problem is Communication with staff. Majority speaks only Chinese. You need some sort of translation app like google translate to help yourself.
Purchase tickets through disney app is recommended - there is promotion when purchasing multiple tickets. Recommend to go on weekdays. The food here is quite nice.

First time here & it was awesome! I spent two days. First day I focused on shows & parades and whatever rides I could squeeze in before opening or that had short lines. The second day I paid for the Premier Pass & got on all the rides I didn’t do done! Totally worth it! It was hot & humid so be prepared! Castle is huge! Must go inside! Pirates of the Caribbean - WOW! Had to do it twice! After the fireworks I ran over to do it again as my last ride of the night! No line! Treasure Cove & all their Pirate Ships & decor were on point! Also, Shanghai is the only other Park that has a Club 33 😉

Took me an hour to enter the park! From where i got off taxi, then queue for bags checking, then entrance 😑 Zootopia is a newly opened area which required 2 hours of queuing into this new area & 1 hour to play the ride. I bought fastpass for $180 & skipped both queuing. Snow white ride was always long wait time, so you can either buy fastpass or wait 150mins+. Tron ride was great! Recommended to play!
Nice experience. It was a little crowded even if we visited it in a rainy December day. But overall the kids were happy.

Visited the Park today at 11am ... Entrance Q was about 1.5 hours as the Park just launched the Zootopia Park Attraction recently. There were many locals wanting to visit the new attraction which added to the larger crowds on this week day. Luckily we pre-booked our entrance tickets and saved at least some time on check-in. Once inside the Park, we were greeted to the beautiful Main Entrance Arch ... retail shops and friendly Staffs. There are 2 hourly interval Road Parades ... occasional Special Events .. which can all be viewed through the Disney App. Given the massive crowd, waiting time for popular rides can take up to 180 minutes !!! We only managed 2 shows and 3 rides in the 12+ hours we were there. Lunch was simple Set bentos, available in many parts of the Park. There are ample toilets and smoking areas. I would strongly recommend downloading the Parks App, which has a Map to help you navigate, show Q-timings in all attractions and other Event information.

One of the Best Days of My Life 🎢🏰 Visiting Shanghai Disney with my family was truly one of the best experiences I’ve ever had. We arrived right when the park opened at 8 AM and didn’t leave until the very end of the day — and still, one day wasn’t enough! Out of all the rides, my favorite was definitely Soaring — it was unforgettable. 💫 There was so much to explore, so many shows and details… I honestly wish I had spent two or even three days there. Shanghai Disney… a dream come true. ❤️

We had a wonderful time. The park is smaller than some other Disney parks but it is loads of fun! We especially enjoyed Tron and the parades, food, as well as hotels are top notch! Plan in advance and if you are a foreigner you need to bring your passport! A favorite is Pirates of the Caribbean ride! It is better than others I have been to at other Disneyland parks, make sure to check it out!

The park is very enormous in size and there are many rides catering to those of all ages. This is, although, not the happiest place on earth, a great way to bond woth family and friends. The queues can get a lil’ too long though.

I arrived at the parking lot and walked about 20 minutes to the park entrance. There’s a Mickey fountain at the entrance. Security checks are similar to other Disney parks; selfie sticks and tripods are prohibited and must be left in lockers, while food and drinks are generally allowed. Entering the park is unique here—you scan your passport, which also serves as your park ticket. You’ll receive a paper ticket with a QR code for reservations, like the Standby Pass for Mickey’s Storybook Adventure. I reserved the 11:40 a.m. show. After entering, I visited Carefree Corner to confirm my Personalized Magical Photo Session, choosing the 4:00 p.m. slot. I then stopped by Avenue M Arcade to buy some Mickey ears for photos and queued up for Mickey’s Storybook Adventure at 10:40 a.m. Shows Mickey’s Storybook Adventure This indoor show takes you through Disney stories with 23 characters. Mickey and Goofy discover a magic book, encountering Olaf, Baloo, King Louie, Moana, Mulan, and others along the way, with live music mainly in Chinese and some English songs. Golden Fairytale Fanfare An outdoor show in front of the Enchanted Storybook Castle featuring Snow White, Elsa, Anna, Jasmine, Aladdin, Ariel, Merida, and more, with English songs. Mickey’s Storybook Express A 14-minute character parade with numerous Disney favorites. ILLUMINATE! A Nighttime Celebration A projection mapping show at the Enchanted Storybook Castle with fireworks, fountains, lasers, and Disney and Marvel characters. Dining Mickey & Pals Market Café • Ma La Tang Noodle Soup with Prawn and Beef (¥119) + Dumplings (¥30) - Spicy, tongue-tingling soup with beef slices and shrimp. • Roasted Spring Chicken with Vegetables (¥129) - Sweet, roasted chicken with a tomato-edamame side. Barbossa’s Bounty • Barbossa Feast for 2 (¥299) - Grilled squid, ribs, and chicken with two servings of rice; overall, it has a sweet flavor. Zootopia Market • Disney Zootopia Pawpsicle (¥45) - A sweet and tangy fruit popsicle, perfect for a warm day. Rides Pirates of the Caribbean Battle for the Sunken Treasure A boat ride through scenes from Pirates of the Caribbean, with forward, backward, and rotating movements. The visuals and sound effects are impressive, and there’s a small wave toward the end, but it’s not intense. Seven Dwarfs Mine Train This ride has a single rider lane, but wait times are similar to the main queue (~1 hour). I bought Disney Premier Access for ¥180, which saved a lot of time. The train takes you through the dwarves’ mine, providing mild thrills. Soaring Over the Horizon Similar to Disney World and DisneySea, this flight simulation ride takes you over global landmarks with scents like grass and ocean waves for an immersive experience. TRON Lightcycle Power Run Experience riding a TRON motorcycle. You lean forward on the bike and hold onto handlebars, speeding along a thrilling track that’s still accessible for younger guests. Zootopia: Hot Pursuit A trackless ride where you pursue runaway sheep from Zootopia. It’s fun, and the single rider line is very short, so I didn’t need to wait. Photo Session After the parade at 3:30 p.m., I headed to Carefree Corner for my photo session. The photographer spoke Chinese, so I used Google Translate to communicate. I requested locations like Gardens of Imagination, Castle Area, Castle Balcony, and Zootopia, and we took photos throughout. With 30 minutes left, I requested to visit Treasure Cove. We wrapped up the session with 100 photos, which were available for download that evening. Note: photos must be downloaded within 90 days, or they’re deleted automatically.

This Disney park has also more to offer for adults than the usual Disneys. During covid-19 times, it is open but required to register and buy ticket in advance. I recommend to buy ticket at least 2-3 days in advance, otherwise it will all be booked, especially on weekends. You cannot buy ticket there, unless there are some free spaces, chances are very low. Also, recommend to download the local Disney app. It has all the maps and information. Since the amount of guests is limited, no need to buy fast lane pass and waiting times are very short compared to usual. The attractions are interactive, but most of them in Chinese only. However you can still understand the context. Don‘t miss the parade (afternoon) and fireworks in the evening! The coolest thing is the park to climb - you can chose the level you want, there are 3 levels from very easy to very hard. You have to leave your stuff in a cabinet you get and you will be secured so there is no risk to fall down. Also, the food there is very tasty and the prices are ok. You can buy very cute Mickey Mouse ice cream or pretzel and pop corn (mostly sweet). The staff there is very friendly and speaks good English. Cool spots to take photos. Very good experience.

3 hours in this park was a punishment! i lived taxi at 9:15 and i was in the at 10:45. 1st you need walk 40min. and you arrive at the 1st check in. they check you and your bag more than am airport. entrance book online only. i don t know the limit acceptable for the park. but minimum wiaiting it s 45 min at 105min entrance 500rmb and if you want one express for one attraction you need pay 180rmb more. a friday in november. i can t imagine during golden in october or under 38⁰C i prefer leave this place 3 hour after my entrance the map was not clear. i went to universal in singapore it was easy to acceed and funny. i will never go to any disney park on the world with children

The theme of the castle at the Shanghai Disneyland is “Enchanted Storybook Castle” it’s also the tallest, largest and most complex Disney castle ever built. And let me tell you, it was beautiful! Instead of a firework show at night they have a marvel themed light show with lasers, fountain lights and some fireworks ofc. It starts at 8:30 and lasts for about 20 mins. There’s a bunch of photographers all through the park just walking around that you can go up to and pay to have your pictures taken professionally. (A whole photoshoot lol) I didn’t so I do not know the exact price. PRO TIP: Get to the front of the castle and get a good seat around 7:30 so you can get the full experience of the light show. It is very cool, they have animations casted onto the castle that are harder to see from the back of the crowd. And if you are seated and need to use the restroom, you can ask the staff to give you a ticket so you can come back and not lose your seat.

This is an excellent place, purely Disney. However, please bear in mind that this place was made for local residents who may not be in a position to travel to America to experience the American parks. Hence, all language, communication and shows are ONLY IN MANDARIN. You will not find anyone able to communicate in English. This place is not for English speaking tourists visiting China. It is purely a Mandarin experience. Wonderfully maintained, great place to cover in a single day.

Excellent work in all the designs, particularly the pirate ship. Black Widow cosplayer was clever and witty. Also enjoyed the buzz lightyear shooting roller coaster. The beauty and the beast castle was well made too.

Shanghai Disneyland is a must-visit (TRON will make you vomit-but-in-a-good-way, Zootopia & Pirates are epic), but be warned: brutal crowds (69k+!), scorching heat (wear sunscreen!), terrible park food (bring snacks!), and rent a stroller unless you want to collapse—still 100% worth it.

A magical and wonderful experience at Shanghai Disneyland! From the start till end of the day, we enjoyed the theme park and reminisced us of our childhood days. Firstly we checked in the Disneyland resort and the staffs there were all friendly and attentive to our accommodations. The check in process was really smooth. After that the magic happened after we went to the land of magic, Disneyland! There were many different attractions/rides inside such as Toy Story, Tron, Pirates of the Caribbean, Zootopia which was exclusively to Shanghai Disneyland currently and many others. All the rides were quite fun and enjoyable for both the young and adults. The staffs there were quite friendly so do not worry to approach them for any queries. Do not miss the fireworks and castle lights display at the end. I think there were 2 timings to the show which was on 8pm and 9pm. There were magnificent and eye opening. The only downside will be the massive crowd which thus contributed to the long waiting times for the rides but this was expected for all great theme parks! Visiting the theme park in the middle of the week will be recommended as I heard that the crowd on the weekends and Monday Friday was much worse. But the crowd were handled well by the borders and the staffs therefore the queue was well managed and orderly. In my opinion, I will certainly recommended all be it families or couples or friends that visited Shanghai to visit Disneyland!

This is the dirtiest Disneyland ever. Trash everywhere. Although they put a lot of trash bin. I think the culture of people just throw trash everywhere. People smoke everywhere. Even the security/cast member were around , but i think they are just not strict in applying the rules. In one of the picture I uploaded shows a man smoking in dining area. Visited Shanghai Disneyland and loved the experience, perhaps it's the use of Chinese/Mandarin letters that made it feel more relatable as an Asian child who worshipped Disney characters growing up. Linguistic Analysis: Code Preference System: The signage at Shanghai Disneyland predominantly displays Chinese text at the top, typically followed by English in a smaller font. This language hierarchy reflects China’s linguistic context, with Chinese as the primary language and English added for accessibility to international visitors. However, a notable deviation in the code preference system appears in the newly opened Zootopia area, where English is displayed more prominently in larger fonts. This choice may be influenced by Zootopia’s strong global appeal and the popularity of its English-language branding, emphasizing an international approach within a largely domestic framework. Inscription system: Signage in the park adjusts its color palette and design to match each themed area’s atmosphere. In Zootopia, signs are bright, bold, and employ contrasting colors to capture the animated, lively essence of the movie. In contrast, signs in the Pirates of the Caribbean area feature neutral, earthy tones that align with the rugged, adventurous theme of the attraction. This thematic alignment in inscription styles not only reinforces the immersive quality of each area but also enhances the overall experience by staying visually consistent with the story world of each ride. Emplacement system: The placement of signage at Shanghai Disneyland is highly strategic, with signs positioned at eye level or above high-traffic areas to ensure maximum visibility in the bustling environment. For instance, in the Pirates of the Caribbean area, directional signs and safety instructions are carefully placed near ride entrances, pathways, and waiting areas. In contrast, the Zootopia area, designed with a playful and vibrant appeal, situates its signs prominently at interactive points, such as character photo spots and attraction entrances.

Another factor that makes this park special is the sheer amount of young people and children dressed up in costumes here. Almost every single child had some sort of cute costumes on. You can also find a lot of attractive young people dressed in Lolita, Gothic, anime, and other creative outfits here. Now about the lines and how to optimize rides. At 8:30am before the park was punblically open, we utilized the early entrance to ride Tron (enough time to ride three rides if you enter at 8am). The park is relatively small so for the rest of the rides you just have to keep an eye on the Disney app and pick times when the wait time is short. Lunch and dinner hours, parade hours, firework hours and after 7:30pm there will be some of the shortest lines, know your priorities and utilize them. When done right you should be able to easily fit 5-8 rides in a day.

The happiest place in Shanghai! It’s the official Disney palace in China. The mouse kingdom has transformed the industrial area in Pudong, Shanghai into a wonderland. There are 2 Disney Resort hotels surrounding the area: Shanghai Disneyland Hotel and Toy Story Hotel. Both are not directly attached to the park like Grand Californian. But as usual their occupancy rate is 90% in average. Normal park opening hours is 8:30 a.m. - 10:00 p.m. This park embraces new technology as part of their flexibility. For example, FastPass can only be used and reserved through the Shanghai Disneyland Resort app, and it’s only available once you enter the park. They even have a timer for when you can take another FastPass. Shanghai Disneyland has 7 themed areas: Mickey Avenue (the mouse king really loves your wallet), Gardens of Imagination, Fantasyland, Treasure Cove, Adventure Isle, Tomorrowland, And Toy Story Land. They are planning to build Zootopia Land sometimes soon. In the morning you can find Mickey and friends eager to take pictures with you around Mickey Avenue. Whereas there are several places specially designed for characters such as Marvel Captain America and Spiderman. The morning dance at the Enchanted Storybook Castle is pretty neat and happened twice in the morning. The parade is fun and happened twice in a day. But the craziest line time is for the 8:30 p.m. fireworks show. As for the rides my favorite has to be Pirates of the Caribbean, just an amazing mixture of water ride with projection mapping story telling plus the sunken boats And the battle against the Kraken. No other pirates ride in all other Disneyland around the world comes close. And of course I must say Tron for the motorbike and rollercoaster fans out there. I went three times in a day for this wonderful ride in Tomorrowland. Honorable mention is the one and only Adventure Isle’s Camp Discovery Challenge Trail. I don’t think this attraction will be allowed in any other Disneyland, it’s a rather dangerous one. Soarin is also available here, but the line is crazy. My suggestion is either you do a FastPass early or go in line early for Soarin. The food in Shanghai Disneyland is absolutely amazing for Disney standards, especially the Chinese cuisine. Don’t forget to grab a bite of Turkey Leg here, they are so juicy compared to other Disneyland.

There are common courtesies that you may expect that do not always exist. For example, Western guests may be shocked in how little personal space exists among the locals. When in line, they will cram up against you in uncomfortable ways.

We purchased our tickets for Disneyland via Klook for a discounted rate around 75 USD each for peak times. For any international visitors you need to have your passport verified as they scan you in. After that you can purchase fastpasses per ride or buy a pack for a handful of rides. On average each fastpass will cost around 10 USD. Lastly, the park unfortunately closes early so they have their main nightly show at 8:30PM and close the park at that time. This show much like the rides incorporates a lot of augmented reality and lights as opposed to a traditional firework show but we really enjoyed the change. The only drawback for me as an American going to a amusement park in China, was the lack of courtesy when standing in line. In America we tend to respect the time the others spent in line. More often than not I've seen people tap the person in front of them so that they'll move ahead as the line moves. In China, you can have stood inline for 50 minutes and stop for 25 seconds to tend to your child and people will rush past you. Not once but multiple times I watched people try to figure out their way around others with children. So stay alert when in lines and keep your entire party together. I just want you to be aware that there are some cultural differences. Also, the PhotoPass it's different from what we're used to at Disney world. They don't have the arm band (your PhotoPass is going to be separate from your room key, which is separate from your ticket to get in to the park). Fastpasses are made at the hotel. You cannot make reservations for restaurant inside the castle without having a pre-purchase ticket for the park, even if you have a Disney hotel reservation.

We went to Shanghai Disneyland on a weekday just after a public holiday and got the Premier Access Pass for all the eligible rides. We managed to go on all the major rides before lunch without wasting any time in queues. For lunch, we ate at the restaurant inside the Pirates of the Caribbean ride, which had a nice atmosphere and was a great spot to relax. After that, we explored the rest of the park and were finished by around 6:00 PM. We even went back for a second go on our favourites — Pirates of the Caribbean and Peter Pan’s Flight. Shanghai Disneyland is a great park—family-friendly, super safe, and full of magic. What really stood out was the staff. They go above and beyond to help, far more friendly and attentive than in other Disney parks I’ve visited. Even when there’s a language barrier, they’ll call someone who speaks English or use translation apps to assist. For example, when we asked about vegetarian options, they went so far as to call the main kitchen to check for us. It was surprising to learn some baked goods, like pretzels and breads, were cooked in lard, but their effort to help us navigate this was truly appreciated. Be prepared for long wait times for rides, though. Bring entertainment for yourself and your kids while you wait—it’s a must. Outside the park, Disneytown offers a range of tea, coffee, snacks, and full meals. It’s a nice place to unwind, but again, the vegetarian options are pretty limited. Overall, the experience was incredible. The kindness and helpfulness of the staff blew us away—nothing like the negative stereotypes you might hear. Shanghai Disneyland is truly worth the visit.
